## Description

<p>Given the <code>head</code> of a singly linked list, reverse the list, and return <em>the reversed list</em>.</p>
<p><strong class="example">Example 1:</strong></p>
![[Personal/LeetCode/Assets/LetCode Assets/reverse-linked-list_0.jpg]]
<pre>
<strong>Input:</strong> head = [1,2,3,4,5]
<strong>Output:</strong> [5,4,3,2,1]
</pre>
<p><strong class="example">Example 2:</strong></p>
![[Personal/LeetCode/Assets/LetCode Assets/reverse-linked-list_1.jpg]]
<pre>
<strong>Input:</strong> head = [1,2]
<strong>Output:</strong> [2,1]
</pre>
<p><strong class="example">Example 3:</strong></p>
<pre>
<strong>Input:</strong> head = []
<strong>Output:</strong> []
</pre>
<p><strong>Constraints:</strong></p>
<ul>
	<li>The number of nodes in the list is the range <code>[0, 5000]</code>.</li>
	<li><code>-5000 &lt;= Node.val &lt;= 5000</code></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Follow up:</strong> A linked list can be reversed either iteratively or recursively. Could you implement both?</p>

---
## Solution

A while loop where we turn each nodes next to previous node should be an easy to implement clean efficient solution for this


So something like 

<div>
<div class="excalidraw-svg excalidraw-dark" style="background-image:url(data:image/svg+xml;base64,);background-size:cover;background-repeat:no-repeat;width:974.6947631835938px;height:auto;aspect-ratio:0.7841681347252539;"></div>
<div class="excalidraw-svg excalidraw-light" style="background-image:url(data:image/svg+xml;base64,);background-size:cover;background-repeat:no-repeat;width:974.6947631835938px;height:auto;aspect-ratio:0.7841681347252539;"></div>
</div>

```python
from algos.linkedlist import Node

def reverse_linkedlist(head: Node) -> Node:
    
    prev = None
    curr = head
    
    while curr:
        nxt = curr.next
        curr.next = prev
        prev = curr
        curr = nxt
        
    return prev
```




```python
v = [1,2,3,4,5]

head = Node.create_linkedlist(v)

head = reverse_linkedlist(head)

head.print_list() # to print the linked list in order
```
